title: Mirror Crystal
summary: Balance a crystal of gems across a diagonal mirror: make a matrix symmetric or skew symmetric, then split it into P + Q.
subject: mathematics
ncertRef: Section 3.6, Symmetric and skew symmetric matrices
concepts: Zero diagonal of a skew matrix
learningOutcome: The student can use A′ = A and A′ = −A to find unknown entries, and write any square matrix as the sum of a symmetric and a skew symmetric matrix.

levels.title: Make it symmetric
levels.adds: Baseline: a symmetric matrix has a_ij = a_ji, so each loose gem equals its reflection across the diagonal (Ex 3.3 Q7, Q8; Misc Q10).
hints: Find the reflection of each loose gem across the main diagonal.
In a symmetric matrix the gem and its reflection are equal.

levels.title: Make it skew
levels.adds: New: a skew symmetric matrix has a_ji = −a_ij, so the diagonal entries are all zero (Ex 3.3 Q7, Q11; Misc Q10).
hints: Each off-diagonal gem is the opposite of its reflection.
A diagonal gem is its own reflection, so a_ii = −a_ii.
The only number equal to its own opposite is 0.

levels.title: Split the crystal
levels.adds: New: A = P + Q with P = ½(A + A′) symmetric and Q = ½(A − A′) skew symmetric (Ex 3.3 Q9, Q10; Example 22).
hints: P’s diagonal gems are the same as A’s.
P is symmetric: its two off-diagonal gems are equal, each the average of A’s two off-diagonal gems.
Q is skew symmetric: its diagonal gems are 0 and its two off-diagonal gems are opposites.
Q’s top right gem is half the difference of A’s off-diagonal gems.

misconceptions: A skew symmetric matrix can have a non-zero diagonal
Every square matrix is either symmetric or skew symmetric
The symmetric part of A is A + A′
